facts.text: There is no standard road traffic in central Venice - vaporetto (water bus) passes are the main public transport, and a multi-day pass is usually better value than paying per ride if moving around a lot.

Sitting at a table (rather than standing at the counter) in most Venetian cafés/bars incurs a significantly higher table-service charge - this is standard and legal, not a scam, but easy to be surprised by.

Restaurants directly on or beside St. Mark's Square and along the main routes to the Rialto Bridge are reliably the most overpriced in the city; Cannaregio and Dorsoduro, away from the main tourist flow, offer better value and quality.
Venice charges a day-tripper access fee on certain peak dates for visitors not staying overnight - check current dates if visiting for a single day rather than staying in the city.
Venice floods periodically ("acqua alta"), most commonly autumn through early spring - raised walkways go up in St. Mark's Square when this happens; it's a normal, managed occurrence, not a crisis.
Venetian cuisine leans heavily on seafood (cicchetti, sarde in saor); vegetarian cicchetti exist but require some seeking out at bacari (wine bars).
